items.question: Attitude to Ukraine, who started the escalation in eastern Ukraine, and what status the Donetsk and Luhansk areas should have.
items.result: In November 2021, 45 percent felt good about Ukraine and 43 percent felt bad. In February 2022, 35 percent felt good and 52 percent felt bad. 60 percent said the United States and NATO countries started the escalation in eastern Ukraine. Before the official status decision, 33 percent said the Donetsk and Luhansk areas should be independent states, 25 percent said they should join Russia, and 26 percent said they should stay part of Ukraine.
items.sample: 1,618 people aged 18 and older, in 137 places and 50 regions, interviewed at home.

items.question: How Russians see Estonia. This page is an interview about a study, not a full results table.
items.result: The page says slightly less than half of respondents called political relations between Russia and Estonia cool, tense, or hostile, and more than half personally feel good about Estonia. 74 percent of those surveyed did not know that an independent Estonian Republic existed before the Second World War. No sample size was printed in the text that was read.

items.question: Name five countries you could call Russia's closest friends and allies. And name five countries you would call the most unfriendly or hostile toward Russia.
items.result: Friends, May 2021: Belarus 58 percent, Ukraine 2 percent, Poland 2 percent. Unfriendly: the United States 66 percent, Ukraine 40 percent, Latvia 21 percent, Poland 21 percent, Lithuania 20 percent, Estonia 9 percent. The printed tables did not list Finland or NATO. 83 percent said Russia has enemies.
items.sample: The page did not print a sample size in the text that was read.
